# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS provides a stable and modern userspace for compilation.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies in a single layer to optimize image size.
# - build-essential: C/C++ compilers and make.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure git clone over HTTPS.
# - cmake: Build system generator for Kripke.
# - git: For cloning the source code.
# - openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI runtime and development headers for MPI support.
# Apt caches are cleaned in the same layer to reduce final image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    && apt-get clean \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a temporary working directory for the build process.
# This directory will be removed after the build is complete.
WORKDIR /tmp/build

# Clone, build, and install Kripke in a single RUN layer.
# This minimizes image layers and cleans up all intermediate build artifacts.
# 1. Clone with --recurse-submodules to fetch the BLT dependency.
# 2. FIX: Use the correct branch name 'master' as 'main' does not exist in the remote repository.
# 3. Create a build subdirectory and configure with CMake for a Release build with MPI enabled.
# 4. Compile the application using all available processor cores for a faster build.
# 5. Copy the 'kripke.exe' executable to '/usr/local/bin/kripke' to place it on the PATH.
# 6. Clean up the entire build directory.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --recurse-submodules --branch master https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git && \
    cd Kripke && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake .. \
        -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
        -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/build

# Reset working directory to a standard location.
WORKDIR /

# Configure Open MPI for containerized/cloud environments.
# This allows mpirun to execute as the root user, a common pattern in Docker containers.

ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# In a Kubernetes environment, you may need to explicitly specify the pod network interface for MPI communication, for example:
# mpirun --mca btl_tcp_if_include eth0 -np <processes> kripke [args]

# Set the default command to show Kripke's help message.
# This serves as a basic health check and demonstrates that the executable is on the PATH.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is configured to deploy the Kripke HPC application
# using the Flux Operator on an AWS CPU instance within a Kubernetes cluster.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for our MiniCluster deployment.
  name: kripke-aws-cpu
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as per instructions.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Defines the number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of parallel tasks (e.g., MPI ranks) for the job.
  tasks: 4

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion to allow for inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Defines the application container(s) to be managed by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to run. The Flux Operator will automatically wrap this with 'flux run'.
      # Kripke is run with no parameters as requested.
      command: kripke
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest is configured to deploy the Kripke HPC application.
# It addresses the previous application-level failure by providing a correct process
# decomposition and targets a high-performance AWS ARM-based Graviton3 instance.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for our MiniCluster deployment.
  name: kripke-aws-cpu
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as per instructions.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Utilize all 64 vCPUs available on the c7g.16xlarge instance.
  tasks: 64

  # Use pod labels for node selection to target the specified AWS instance type.
  # This ensures the job runs on the powerful ARM-based c7g.16xlarge instance.
  jobLabels:
    node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7g.16xlarge

  # Configure the Flux framework itself for the ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Specify the ARM-compatible Flux container image.
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion to allow for inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Defines the application container to be managed by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to run. This now includes the '--procs' flag to correctly
      # decompose the problem across the 64 MPI tasks (4x4x4=64), resolving
      # the previous assertion failure.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4

      launcher: false
